sentences.en: What’s their secret? This is Hidden Brain, I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 他们的秘诀是什么？这里是 Hidden Brain，我是 Shankar Vedantam。

sentences.en: In October 1967, the world's greatest chess minds gathered in Sousse, Tunisia, to face off at the Interzonal Tournament, the high stakes gateway to the World Chess Championship.
sentences.zh: 1967年10月，世界上最顶尖的国际象棋高手齐聚突尼斯苏塞，参加区际赛——那是通往世界国际象棋锦标赛的高风险门槛赛事。

sentences.en: The early games were dominated by the American prodigy Bobby Fischer.
sentences.zh: 赛事早期的对局，由美国天才棋手鲍比·菲舍尔主导。

sentences.en: He was a 24-year-old grandmaster with an IQ rumored to be at the genius level of 180.
sentences.zh: 他当时24岁，已是特级大师，据传智商高达180，属于天才级别。

sentences.en: He was the favorite to win it all.
sentences.zh: 他是夺冠的头号热门。

sentences.en: But despite his overwhelming lead, the tournament quickly spiraled into a master class in self-sabotage.
sentences.zh: 但尽管遥遥领先，这场比赛却很快演变成了一堂关于自我毁灭的“大师课”。

sentences.en: Bobby Fischer issued a series of escalating demands regarding his playing schedule.
sentences.zh: 鲍比·菲舍尔就自己的比赛日程，提出了一连串不断升级的要求。

sentences.en: When organizers refused to rearrange the event to suit him, he walked out, withdrawing from the tournament while in first place and throwing away years of work in a single fit of frustration.
sentences.zh: 当组委会拒绝为迁就他而调整赛程时，他愤然离场，在自己领先的情况下退出了比赛，一时的挫败情绪，就这样葬送了多年的心血。

sentences.en: The walkout was a window into a profound emotional ineptness that lived right alongside Bobby Fischer's brilliance.
sentences.zh: 这次退赛，让人们窥见了鲍比·菲舍尔身上，与他的天赋并存的那种深深的情感笨拙。

sentences.en: Throughout his career, he operated in a state of constant relational friction, alienating the very coaches and friends who tried to support him.
sentences.zh: 在他的整个职业生涯中，他始终处于人际摩擦不断的状态，把那些想要支持他的教练和朋友一个个都推开了。

sentences.en: At his chess matches, he frequently violated the social norms of the game, arriving late and refusing to make eye contact with the player sitting across from him.
sentences.zh: 在比赛中，他常常违反棋坛的社交礼仪，迟到，还拒绝与坐在对面的棋手有任何眼神接触。

sentences.en: Bobby Fischer possessed a mind that could see a dozen moves ahead on a chessboard, but he struggled with the basic moves of social and emotional life.
sentences.zh: 鲍比·菲舍尔的头脑，能在棋盘上预判十几步棋，可在社交和情感生活最基本的“落子”上，他却举步维艰。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain and in a companion episode on Hidden Brain Plus, the logic of emotion and how feelings make us smarter.
sentences.zh: 本周的 Hidden Brain，以及 Hidden Brain Plus 的配套节目，我们要聊的是情绪的逻辑，以及感受如何让我们变得更聪明。

sentences.en: For moi. Think back to the last time you made a decision you regretted.
sentences.zh: 对我来说也是如此。回想一下，你上一次做出让自己后悔的决定，是什么时候。

sentences.en: Perhaps you fell blinded by rage or paralyzed by fear.
sentences.zh: 也许你曾被愤怒蒙蔽，或是被恐惧困住。

sentences.en: In those moments, it feels like our emotions are obstacles to our success, a vestige of our primitive brains getting in the way of our rational minds.
sentences.zh: 在那些时刻，我们会觉得情绪是通往成功的绊脚石，是原始大脑残留下来、妨碍理性思维的东西。

sentences.en: But research in recent decades into the world of emotions suggests that this idea is profoundly wrong.
sentences.zh: 但近几十年关于情绪世界的研究表明，这种看法是大错特错的。

sentences.en: Emotions are central to our ability to understand, attend and to prioritize.
sentences.zh: 情绪对我们理解事物、集中注意力、判断优先级的能力，都至关重要。

sentences.en: They aren't obstacles that block our path.
sentences.zh: 它们不是挡在我们前进路上的障碍。

sentences.en: They are food and fuel for the journey. Peter Salovey is a psychologist at Yale University.
sentences.zh: 它们是这段旅程的食粮与燃料。彼得·萨洛维是耶鲁大学的一位心理学家。

sentences.en: He studies how our emotions shape our decisions and our behavior.
sentences.zh: 他研究的是我们的情绪如何塑造我们的决策和行为。

sentences.en: Peter Salovey, welcome to Hidden Brain. Thank you so much, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 彼得·萨洛维，欢迎来到 Hidden Brain。非常感谢，Shankar。

sentences.en: It's a real honor to be with you. I listen to your show regularly and have enjoyed seeing you live as well.
sentences.zh: 能和你在一起，真的很荣幸。我经常收听你的节目，也很喜欢看你的现场活动。

sentences.en: And so it's a privilege to be a guest.
sentences.zh: 所以能来做客，我深感荣幸。

sentences.en: Peter, in addition to being a psychology professor at Yale, you've held several administrative posts at the university, including provost and dean.
sentences.zh: 彼得，你除了是耶鲁大学的心理学教授，还在学校担任过好几个行政职务，包括教务长和院长。

sentences.en: While you were dean, a prominent individual visited the campus.
sentences.zh: 你担任院长期间，有一位重要人物到访过校园。

sentences.en: Can you paint me a picture of the moment you got to shake hands with the president?
sentences.zh: 你能给我描述一下，你和这位总统握手那一刻的情景吗？

sentences.en: Yes, we had invited President Clinton to visit campus.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们邀请了克林顿总统来校园访问。

sentences.en: And if memory serves, he was going to give a talk on campus at the time.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，他当时是要在校园里发表演讲。

sentences.en: And they lined all of us up, all the deans in the boardroom, actually, of the university.
sentences.zh: 他们把我们所有人排成一排，其实就是学校所有的院长，都站在会议室里。

sentences.en: We were around the perimeter, and President Clinton walked in.
sentences.zh: 我们围成一圈站着，克林顿总统走了进来。

sentences.en: And he worked his way around the perimeter of the room, shaking hands with everyone.
sentences.zh: 他沿着房间的四周走了一圈，逐一和大家握手。

sentences.en: And when he got to me, I was quite nervous, actually.
sentences.zh: 轮到我的时候，说实话，我相当紧张。

sentences.en: And he stuck out his hands and he said, I'm Bill Clinton.
sentences.zh: 他伸出手说，我是比尔·克林顿。

sentences.en: And I said, I'm Peter Salovey. I'm the Dean of Yale College.
sentences.zh: 我说，我是彼得·萨洛维，我是耶鲁学院的院长。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, it's a pleasure to meet you, Peter.
sentences.zh: 他说，很高兴见到你，彼得。

sentences.en: We actually already know each other.
sentences.zh: 我们其实早就认识了。

sentences.en: So when he said that you had met earlier, had you actually met him earlier, Peter?
sentences.zh: 那么，当他说你们之前见过面时，彼得，你们真的早些时候见过吗？

sentences.en: No, I had never met him, at least, you know, not to my memory, but no, no, I had never met him.
sentences.zh: 没有，我从没见过他，至少据我所知没有，是的，我确实从未见过他。

sentences.en: I had never met him. And so I was surprised when he said that.
sentences.zh: 我从未见过他。所以他这么说的时候，我很惊讶。

sentences.en: And of course, I was a little nervous, like am I, I forget that I had met Bill Clinton?
sentences.zh: 当然，我也有点紧张，心想，难道我见过比尔·克林顿却忘了？

sentences.en: How could that possibly be? So I'm a little self-conscious in my interaction at that point.
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能呢？所以那一刻我在互动中显得有点不自在。

sentences.en: So something happened earlier that day that is pertinent to what Bill Clinton told you.
sentences.zh: 所以那天早些时候发生了一件事，和比尔·克林顿对你说的那句话有关。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened earlier that morning, Peter.
sentences.zh: 彼得，跟我说说那天早上发生了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, so as I was coming on the campus, really to park near where this meet and greet was going to take place, I saw a spot, I pulled in quickly, and I didn't realize it, but I had pulled right in front of Bill Clinton's limo.
sentences.zh: 是这样的，我当时开车到校园，想把车停在见面活动附近的地方，看见一个车位，就很快地把车开了进去，但我没意识到，我正好停在了比尔·克林顿的豪华轿车前面。

sentences.en: And in fact, kind of cut it off. And a Secret Service agent, or some kind of security that was with him, jumped out of the car and said, wait, wait, wait, wait, wait.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，等于是截住了他的车。他身边的一名特勤局特工，或者说某种安保人员，一下子从车里跳出来说，等等、等等、等等、等等。

sentences.en: And President Clinton rolled the window down and said, no, no, no, no, it's okay.
sentences.zh: 克林顿总统摇下车窗说，不、不、不、不，没关系。

sentences.en: That guy is the Dean. And I realized he had been reviewing the people he was going to meet in his car, most likely, as a public figure might.
sentences.zh: 那位是院长。我意识到，他很可能像公众人物常做的那样，坐在车里的时候已经先看过了他要见的这些人的资料。

sentences.en: And so when I was in the meet and greet line to meet him, he said to me, we already know each other.
sentences.zh: 所以当我排队等着和他见面握手时，他对我说，我们已经认识了。

sentences.en: And I was so charmed by this. And more importantly, he could tell I was nervous.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得他这样说真是很有魅力。更重要的是，他看出了我很紧张。

sentences.en: You could tell I was anxious meeting the president.
sentences.zh: 他看得出我在见总统这件事上很焦虑。

sentences.en: And he told that story to sort of say, there's no need to be nervous, Mr.
sentences.zh: 他讲那个故事，其实是想说，没必要紧张，先生……

sentences.en: Dean. We're old friends. We had an interaction earlier today.
sentences.zh: 院长。我们是老朋友了，我们今天早些时候已经打过交道了。

sentences.en: It put me at ease. It was a wonderful example of President Clinton managing my emotions.
sentences.zh: 这让我一下子放松下来。这是克林顿总统调节我情绪的一个绝佳例子。

sentences.en: He could see I'm nervous. No need to be nervous.
sentences.zh: 他看出我很紧张，就说没必要紧张。

sentences.en: We're old friends, he says. And in fact, the old friends is based on an embarrassing interaction, but that doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们是老朋友。而事实上，所谓“老朋友”，是建立在一次略显尴尬的交集之上的，但那都不重要了。

sentences.en: I've seen photographs of the moment. He's looking me in the eye and giving me a firm handshake.
sentences.zh: 我见过那一刻的照片。他直视着我的眼睛，用力地和我握手。

sentences.en: And it's that when he's looking at me, he is seeing that I have a look of nervousness or fear or anxiety in my face.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，他看着我的时候，能看出我脸上流露出紧张、害怕或焦虑的神情。

sentences.en: And it cues him to do something, which is tell this story about the interaction with him and his limo in the Secret Service, because he knows it might put me at ease, or at least make us feel familiar and like old, old friends.
sentences.zh: 这促使他做了一件事，就是讲了那个关于他的轿车和特勤局特工的小插曲，因为他知道，这也许能让我放松下来，至少能让我们感觉彼此熟络，像老朋友一样。

sentences.en: What Peter realized after the fact was that Bill Clinton had demonstrated an essential idea in Peter's own research.
sentences.zh: 彼得事后才意识到，比尔·克林顿当时展现出的，正是他自己研究中的一个核心理念。

sentences.en: Some people are incredibly skilled at reading a room.
sentences.zh: 有些人特别擅长“读懂一个房间”的氛围。

sentences.en: In interactions with others, this gives them an edge.
sentences.zh: 在与他人的互动中，这会给他们带来明显的优势。

sentences.en: They can see around the corners of a conversation, soothe frictions, put people at ease.
sentences.zh: 他们能看透对话背后的弯弯绕绕，抚平摩擦，让人安心。

sentences.en: Some years after this incident, Peter became a president himself.
sentences.zh: 这件事过后几年，彼得自己也当上了校长。

sentences.en: He became president of Yale. He inherited a challenge that required the same skills of him that Bill Clinton had shown in that interaction.
sentences.zh: 他成了耶鲁大学的校长。他所面对的一个挑战，恰恰需要用到克林顿当年在那次互动中展现出的那种能力。

sentences.en: We had a residential college named for John C.
sentences.zh: 我们有一所住宿学院，是以约翰·C·

sentences.en: Calhoun.
sentences.zh: 卡尔霍恩的名字命名的。

sentences.en: John C. Calhoun was a senator, was the vice president of the United States all before the Civil War, served as, I think, secretary of state and secretary of war as well.
sentences.zh: 约翰·C·卡尔霍恩曾是参议员，在南北战争之前担任过美国副总统，我记得他还担任过国务卿和陆军部长。

sentences.en: But what he was most well-known for is his ardent defense of slavery.
sentences.zh: 但他最广为人知的，是他对奴隶制度的坚定捍卫。

sentences.en: Slavery not just as a, quote, way of life in the South, but to use his words, as a positive good.
sentences.zh: 他不只是把奴隶制说成南方的一种“生活方式”，而是用他自己的话说，是一种“积极的善”。

sentences.en: He believed, and he rooted it in white supremacy.
sentences.zh: 他这样相信，而且这种信念根植于白人至上主义。

sentences.en: He viewed it as the proper order of society.
sentences.zh: 他把这看作是社会应有的秩序。

sentences.en: And I imagine he must have gone to Yale himself if a building was named after him.
sentences.zh: 我猜，既然有一栋楼以他命名，他本人应该也曾就读于耶鲁吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, he had been vice president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 是的，他曾担任美国副总统。

sentences.en: He was a Yale graduate. And when the building was built in about 1930, there was a debate about who to name it for.
sentences.zh: 他是耶鲁大学的毕业生。这栋楼大约建于1930年，当时关于用谁的名字命名，曾有过一番争论。

sentences.en: And there were two colleges being named that year, and they named one of the colleges after a minister.
sentences.zh: 那一年有两所学院要命名，其中一所以一位牧师的名字命名。

sentences.en: And so the other was to be named after the most prominent statesman, who at the time would have been John C.
sentences.zh: 于是另一所，就打算以当时最有名望的政治家来命名，而那个人，正是约翰·C·

sentences.en: Calhoun. So with that as history, over the years, many decades, there had been more and less protest about this name.
sentences.zh: 卡尔霍恩。有了这段历史，多年来，几十年间，围绕这个名字，陆续出现过或多或少的抗议。

sentences.en: Why do we name a college after the most ardent defender of slavery?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要用一个最坚定的奴隶制捍卫者的名字来命名一所学院呢？

sentences.en: And so I, in some ways, tired of receiving petitions about this or watching protest, I said, let's have a conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种程度上，我已经厌倦了不断收到相关请愿、目睹抗议，于是我说，我们来谈一谈吧。

sentences.en: And I gave my welcoming speech that fall.
sentences.zh: 那年秋天，我发表了开学致辞。

sentences.en: And I said, let's have the kind of conversations you should have on campus about whether we should continue to have a college named for John C.
sentences.zh: 我说，我们应该在校园里展开这样一场对话：我们是否应该继续保留以约翰·C·

sentences.en: Kellen. And I made the argument that good people, moral people, thoughtful people, would likely find themselves on both sides of this issue.
sentences.zh: 卡尔霍恩命名的这所学院。我当时提出的论点是，善良的人、有道德的人、有思想的人，很可能会在这个问题上站在对立的两边。

sentences.en: Some wanting change, some saying we don't need to honor John C.
sentences.zh: 有人希望改变，有人说我们没必要去纪念约翰·C·

sentences.en: Kellen, and others saying we may not agree with John C.
sentences.zh: 卡尔霍恩，还有人说，我们或许并不认同约翰·C·

sentences.en: Kellen, but he's a public figure, a historic figure, and universities should not be in the business of effacing history.
sentences.zh: 卡尔霍恩，但他是一位公众人物，一位历史人物，大学不应该以抹去历史为己任。

sentences.en: So, early on, as this controversy was brewing, you decided that the name should not be changed.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这场争议刚刚酝酿的时候，你就决定不改这个名字。

sentences.en: Talk about the moment you actually announced this to the campus and what the reaction was, Peter.
sentences.zh: 彼得，说说你正式向校园宣布这个决定的那一刻，以及当时的反应吧。

sentences.en: Sure. While our students generally wanted the name to be changed, our alumni did not, and our faculty at that point were largely not interested in this particular issue.
sentences.zh: 好的。当时我们的学生普遍希望改名，但我们的校友不希望，而我们的教师当时大多对这个具体议题并不太关心。

sentences.en: And I talked to many experts, the head of the NAACP, prominent African American intellectuals who had lived in Calhoun College when they were Yale undergraduates, and many, many others.
sentences.zh: 我和很多专家交流过，包括全国有色人种协进会的负责人，一些曾在耶鲁读本科时住在卡尔霍恩学院的著名非裔美国知识分子，还有很多很多其他人。

sentences.en: And all of them were profoundly ambivalent about the idea of a facing history.
sentences.zh: 他们所有人，对于“直面历史”这个说法，都抱有一种深深的矛盾心理。

sentences.en: We should leave his name on there, many of them said, but confront him in other ways.
sentences.zh: 他们中很多人说，我们应该保留他的名字，但要用别的方式去正视他。

sentences.en: And so in light of that, I had announced that we would maintain the name, but we would contextualize it.
sentences.zh: 有鉴于此，我宣布我们将保留这个名字，但会为它加上历史语境的说明。

sentences.en: We would put up educational materials plaques and the like, explaining who he was and what he believed and why we left his name on the college.
sentences.zh: 我们会设置一些教育性的说明牌匾之类的东西，解释他是谁、他信奉什么，以及我们为什么保留他的名字在这所学院上。

sentences.en: Well, I think the next day after announcing that decision, there was a very loud protest on campus led by students.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我记得宣布这个决定后的第二天，校园里就爆发了一场由学生主导的、声势浩大的抗议。

sentences.en: We had a town hall meeting at which I spoke, and now the faculty were quite energized by the issue.
sentences.zh: 我们举行了一场市政厅式的会议，我在会上发了言，这时候教师们也一下子被这件事调动起来了。

sentences.en: I think seeing how upset the students were, they were then calling for a different outcome.
sentences.zh: 我想，看到学生们如此激动，他们随即也开始呼吁一个不同的结果。

sentences.en: I understand that during the town hall, there was a moment when students were showering you with fake cash to make the assertion that you cared more about donors and the alumni than the well-being of students.
sentences.zh: 我了解到，在那场市政厅会议上，曾有一个时刻，学生们朝你身上撒假钞，以此表达一种指控：你更在乎捐赠者和校友，而不是学生的福祉。

sentences.en: And that must have come as something of a shock to you.
sentences.zh: 那对你来说想必是相当大的冲击。

sentences.en: That of course was a shock to me. You know, I was a very student-oriented president.
sentences.zh: 那当然是给了我不小的冲击。要知道，我一直是一位非常重视学生的校长。

sentences.en: I taught students introductory psychology for many, many, many years.
sentences.zh: 我教了学生很多很多年的心理学入门课程。

sentences.en: And so I was not happy about that kind of protest.
sentences.zh: 所以对于那样的抗议，我心里并不好受。

sentences.en: Several months later, in the summer, a worker in Calhoun College, I believe he was a dining hall worker, noticed that the iconography, the symbolism, the windows, stained-glass windows, in Calhoun College reflected themes relevant to the name.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，到了夏天，卡尔霍恩学院的一名工作人员——我记得他是食堂的员工——注意到学院里的图像、象征符号，那些彩绘玻璃窗，映照着与这个名字相关的主题。

sentences.en: They reflected the old South, African Americans picking cotton.
sentences.zh: 那些图案描绘的是旧南方，是非裔美国人在地里采摘棉花的场景。

sentences.en: John C. Calhoun is kind of a statesman looking regal.
sentences.zh: 约翰·C·卡尔霍恩则被塑造成一位仪态威严的政治家形象。

sentences.en: And he, in a kind of emotional moment, he broke one of these stained-glass windows, I believe it was the one of the African Americans picking cotton.
sentences.zh: 他在一种情绪激动的时刻，打碎了其中一扇彩绘玻璃窗，我记得就是那扇描绘非裔美国人采棉花的窗户。

sentences.en: And he said that as a black man, I couldn't stand looking at that every day.
sentences.zh: 他说，作为一个黑人，他没办法忍受每天都看着那样的画面。

sentences.en: And I needed to do something.
sentences.zh: 他必须做点什么。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, Peter, as you heard about all this protest, and you saw how intense the feelings were, did you have a moment when you felt that you had in some ways misjudged the intensity, the depth of feelings that existed on campus about this Yes, and I think part of that was that times were changing.
sentences.zh: 彼得，我很好奇，当你听到这一系列抗议、看到大家的情绪如此激烈时，你是否有过这样一个时刻：觉得自己在某种程度上，低估了校园里这种情绪的强度和深度？是的，我想部分原因在于，时代正在变化。

sentences.en: This was all happening in a dynamic environment.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是在一个不断变化的环境中发生的。

sentences.en: It was happening in real time. And I think when we began this conversation, sure, students wanted change, but many other people quite reasonably made the argument that a facing history was not appropriate.
sentences.zh: 事情是实时发生、不断演进的。我想，当我们刚开始这场讨论时，学生们固然想要改变，但也有很多人相当合理地提出，直面历史并不意味着一定要改名。

sentences.en: I think views shifted over the course of that year.
sentences.zh: 我想，在那一年的进程中，大家的看法逐渐发生了转变。

sentences.en: And in the course of grappling with my own feelings about that, I met with an African American student who grew up in South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 在努力梳理自己对这件事的感受的过程中，我见到了一位在南卡罗来纳州长大的非裔美国学生。

sentences.en: In fact, she grew up, I believe, in a home just off of Calhoun Street in Charleston.
sentences.zh: 事实上，据我所知，她就是在查尔斯顿卡尔霍恩街附近的一户人家长大的。

sentences.en: This student said to me something very interesting.
sentences.zh: 这位学生对我说了一句很触动我的话。

sentences.en: She said, I've known the name of Calhoun all my life.
sentences.zh: 她说，我一辈子都知道卡尔霍恩这个名字。

sentences.en: I know who he is. I can handle being in a space named for John C.
sentences.zh: 我知道他是谁。我可以接受生活在一个以约翰·C·

sentences.en: Calhoun such as Calhoun College.
sentences.zh: 卡尔霍恩命名的空间里，比如卡尔霍恩学院。

sentences.en: But I don't want to live in a shrine to slavery.
sentences.zh: 但我不愿意生活在一座奴隶制的神龛里。

sentences.en: And I said, that's a powerful metaphor. What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 我说，这是一个很有力的比喻。你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: She goes, look at the stained glass windows.
sentences.zh: 她说，你去看看那些彩绘玻璃窗吧。

sentences.en: Look at the reliefs carved into the stone walls.
sentences.zh: 你去看看那些雕刻在石墙上的浮雕吧。

sentences.en: Look at the artifacts from plantations in the south that are in the collection of this college.
sentences.zh: 你去看看学院收藏里那些来自南方种植园的文物吧。

sentences.en: Look at the name that is on our t-shirts when we go out and play intramural sports.
sentences.zh: 你去看看我们出去打校内体育比赛时，T恤上印着的那个名字吧。

sentences.en: This has become a shrine to slavery.
sentences.zh: 这里已经成了一座奴隶制的神龛。

sentences.en: And I swallowed hard, and I had a moment of emotional understanding and deep empathy.
sentences.zh: 我当时使劲咽了口口水，那一刻，我获得了一种情感上的理解，一种深切的共情。

sentences.en: That the debate really wasn't entirely about, do you honor figures from the past, even if we completely disavow their viewpoints now?
sentences.zh: 这场争论其实从来都不只是关于：我们是否应该纪念过去的人物，即便我们如今已经完全否定他们的观点？

sentences.en: Or whether you have faced history, or whether times change and who we honor should change?
sentences.zh: 或者说，我们是否真正直面了历史，抑或时代变了，我们所纪念的人也应该随之而变？

sentences.en: I suddenly got focused on how people feel.
sentences.zh: 我突然把关注点，转向了人们的真实感受。

sentences.en: Thinking about that student living in a shrine to slavery, thinking about our worker so moved to an act of vandalism that he risked his job, he risked criminal prosecution, it was a shift in my thinking.
sentences.zh: 想到那位生活在“奴隶制神龛”中的学生，想到那位工作人员被触动到不惜冒着丢掉工作、甚至面临刑事指控的风险去做出破坏行为，我的想法发生了转变。

sentences.en: And it was really a processing of those emotions, triggered by my interaction with the student primarily, that created a moment of clarity for me and suggested that we needed to consider an alternative path.
sentences.zh: 而真正让我豁然开朗、觉得我们需要考虑另一条路的，正是这些情绪的沉淀——主要是由我和那位学生的交流所触发的。

sentences.en: What did you end up doing? We ended up changing the name.
sentences.zh: 那你最后是怎么做的？我们最终还是改了这个名字。

sentences.en: The name of that college is Grace Hopper College, named after an early computer scientist, I think before the field had even been invented, and a Navy Admiral.
sentences.zh: 那所学院现在叫格蕾丝·霍珀学院，是以一位早期的计算机科学家命名的——我想那时候这个学科甚至还没有真正诞生——同时她也是一位海军将官。

sentences.en: But we honored her service and being one of the early founders of the field.
sentences.zh: 我们是在表彰她的贡献，表彰她是这个领域的早期奠基人之一。

sentences.en: She had gotten her PhD in mathematics at Yale.
sentences.zh: 她曾在耶鲁获得数学博士学位。

sentences.en: But it was really this moment of insight created by the arousal of empathy following an emotional conversation with a student that set me anyway on a different course in my thinking.
sentences.zh: 但真正让我在思考上走上一条不同道路的，其实是那次与一位学生的情感对话所激发出的共情，以及由此产生的顿悟时刻。

sentences.en: One of the most consequential challenges we face in daily life is to read what is happening in the emotional lives of other people.
sentences.zh: 我们在日常生活中面对的最重要的挑战之一，就是去读懂他人情感世界里正在发生的事。

sentences.en: When we come back, how the ability to read the emotional undercurrents in a room can transform our lives.
sentences.zh: 节目稍后回来，我们将聊聊读懂一个房间里情绪暗流的能力，如何能改变我们的人生。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain. I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是 Hidden Brain，我是 Shankar Vedantam。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain. I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 这里是 Hidden Brain，我是 Shankar Vedantam。

sentences.en: Schools and universities often test students on their knowledge of complex material.
sentences.zh: 学校和大学常常通过复杂知识的测验来考核学生。

sentences.en: In the workplace, employees are promoted because of their expertise and problem-solving skills.
sentences.zh: 在职场中，员工凭借专业能力和解决问题的技能获得晋升。

sentences.en: We've all heard of geniuses who produce great works of literature or magnificent musical compositions.
sentences.zh: 我们都听说过那些创作出伟大文学作品或壮丽音乐作品的天才。

sentences.en: But dig a layer deeper, and you find that some of the smartest people are not very smart when it comes to gauging the emotional temperature of a situation.
sentences.zh: 但再往深挖一层就会发现，有些最聪明的人，在判断一个场合的情绪温度时，其实并不怎么“聪明”。

sentences.en: When they meet someone new, they find it hard to tell a friend from foe.
sentences.zh: 他们在认识新朋友的时候，很难分辨对方是友是敌。

sentences.en: They are unaware of the emotional undercurrents swirling around them, and they often behave like bulls in china shops.
sentences.zh: 他们对周围涌动的情绪暗流毫无察觉，行事常常就像闯进瓷器店的公牛。

sentences.en: Peter Salovey is a psychologist at Yale University.
sentences.zh: 彼得·萨洛维是耶鲁大学的一位心理学家。

sentences.en: He studies how our emotions shape our decisions and our behavior.
sentences.zh: 他研究的是我们的情绪如何塑造我们的决策和行为。

sentences.en: Peter, your research tackles a long-standing belief of Western culture, that thinking and feeling are opposing forces in the mind.
sentences.zh: 彼得，你的研究挑战了西方文化中一个由来已久的信念，那就是：理性与情感是心智中相互对立的两股力量。

sentences.en: Talk a moment about the long history of that idea.
sentences.zh: 跟我们聊聊这个观念的悠久历史吧。

sentences.en: Yes. Whether you're looking at stoic philosophers or many religious traditions and the like, the idea is that we shouldn't be ruled by our passions.
sentences.zh: 好的。无论是看斯多葛学派的哲学家，还是众多宗教传统等等，其中的观念都是：我们不该被自己的激情所支配。

sentences.en: You know, rule your feelings or your feelings will rule you, is kind of the idea.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那种“驾驭你的情绪，否则情绪就会驾驭你”的说法，大概就是这个意思。

sentences.en: That on the one hand, we have thought and reason, and on the other, we have emotions, passions.
sentences.zh: 一方面，我们有思想和理性；另一方面，我们有情绪和激情。

sentences.en: The belief was somehow that our emotions were vestigial, meaning, yes, they're part of our animal heritage, just like our wisdom teeth, just like our appendices.
sentences.zh: 这种信念在某种程度上认为，我们的情绪是一种“退化的遗迹”——也就是说，没错，它们是我们动物性遗产的一部分，就像我们的智齿，就像我们的阑尾一样。

sentences.en: But we don't really need them anymore. We are a thinking species.
sentences.zh: 但我们其实已经不再真正需要它们了。我们是一个会思考的物种。

sentences.en: Peter and a colleague, Jack Mayer, noticed there were all kinds of situations where people are asked to read the emotional temperature of a situation.
sentences.zh: 彼得和他的同事杰克·迈耶注意到，在各种各样的场合中，人们都被要求去读懂一个情境的情绪温度。

sentences.en: Some people are better at doing this than others.
sentences.zh: 有些人在这方面比其他人更擅长。

sentences.en: Wasn't this a kind of intelligence too? They wondered.
sentences.zh: 他们不禁想，这难道不也是一种智力吗？

sentences.en: Together, they came up with a formulation for the skill they were talking about.
sentences.zh: 他们一起，为这种他们所讨论的能力，提出了一套阐述。

sentences.en: They called it emotional intelligence. The idea came to them in the artist of places.
sentences.zh: 他们把它称为“情商”。而这个想法，是在一个意想不到的地方冒出来的。

sentences.en: Not a lab, but as the two were painting Peter's living room.
sentences.zh: 不是在实验室里，而是在他们两人一起粉刷彼得家客厅的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is what happened. And we're painting the living room.
sentences.zh: 是的，事情就是这样发生的。我们当时在粉刷客厅。

sentences.en: We're talking about emotions. We're talking about intelligence.
sentences.zh: 我们聊着情绪，聊着智力。

sentences.en: We both had done research on the impact of mood and emotion on memory, on judgment, on decision making.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都做过关于情绪和心境如何影响记忆、判断和决策的研究。

sentences.en: And we're just chatting as we paint it. Jack was very nice to help me paint my living room.
sentences.zh: 我们就那样一边刷墙一边闲聊。杰克人很好，特意来帮我粉刷客厅。

sentences.en: We'd only been friends a year or two at that point.
sentences.zh: 那时候我们才认识一两年，还只是朋友。

sentences.en: And talked about this idea of emotional intelligence.
sentences.zh: 然后就聊到了“情商”这个想法。

sentences.en: My original idea was let's develop a framework for organizing all of these abilities having to do with the emotions and their effect on thinking and behavior.
sentences.zh: 我最初的想法是，我们应该建立一个框架，把所有这些与情绪有关、并影响思维和行为的能力都组织起来。

sentences.en: Jack came out of a more traditional intelligence laboratory, but had now turned his attention to mood and emotion.
sentences.zh: 杰克出身于一个更传统的智力研究实验室，但当时已经把研究方向转向了心境和情绪。

sentences.en: And he was wondering whether you could measure any of this.
sentences.zh: 他当时在想，这些东西是不是可以被测量出来。

sentences.en: And so we came together in that way, yes, and it was while painting my house.
sentences.zh: 于是我们就这样走到了一起，没错，就是在粉刷我家房子的时候。

sentences.en: Peter and his colleagues have found ways to measure emotional intelligence.
sentences.zh: 彼得和他的同事们后来找到了测量情商的方法。

sentences.en: Instead of asking people about their emotional skills, people turn out to be poor judges of their own emotional intelligence.
sentences.zh: 与其直接去问人们自己的情感能力如何，不如说，事实证明，人们很难准确判断自己的情商。

sentences.en: The researchers came up with a series of tests.
sentences.zh: 研究者们设计出了一系列测验。

sentences.en: How good were people at reading the expressions of others?
sentences.zh: 人们在解读他人表情方面的能力究竟如何？

sentences.en: How well did they understand what was happening in their own emotional lives?
sentences.zh: 他们对自己内心的情感生活，理解得又有多好？

sentences.en: How skillful were they at regulating their emotions?
sentences.zh: 他们在调节自己情绪方面，又有多熟练？

sentences.en: They came up with a measure, very much like an IQ test.
sentences.zh: 他们设计出了一套测量方法，很像一种智商测验。

sentences.en: It came to be called the Meyer-Salovey-Caruso Scale, or Mesquite for short.
sentences.zh: 这套测验后来被称为“梅耶-萨洛维-卡鲁索量表”，简称 MSCEIT。

sentences.en: We did a study in which you came to the lab as a participant in research and had to interact with a stranger.
sentences.zh: 我们做过一项研究，让参与者来到实验室，与一位陌生人互动。

sentences.en: And then the stranger would rate how well did you listen to him?
sentences.zh: 然后由那位陌生人来评价：你听他说话听得有多用心？

sentences.en: How connected were you trying to be with him?
sentences.zh: 你在多大程度上努力与他建立连接？

sentences.en: How empathic did you seem? And for our participants who scored well on the Mesquite, the stranger rated them more highly.
sentences.zh: 你表现得有多有同理心？结果发现，那些在 MSCEIT 测验中得分较高的参与者，会得到陌生人更高的评价。

sentences.en: But also, we could show videos of that interaction to others, who had no idea, of course, what the experiment really was about.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们还可以把这段互动的录像放给其他人看，那些人完全不知道这个实验到底是关于什么的。

sentences.en: And they rated the person as more sociable, better able to make friends, and the like.
sentences.zh: 他们同样会认为，得分更高的人更善于社交、更容易交到朋友，诸如此类。

sentences.en: If they had higher scores. We could also do just correlational studies.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以做纯粹的相关性研究。

sentences.en: How many friends do you have? It's predicted by the Mesquite, by our emotional intelligence measure.
sentences.zh: 你有多少朋友？这也能由 MSCEIT，也就是我们的情商测量工具，预测出来。

sentences.en: Do you engage in pro-social behaviors with friends?
sentences.zh: 你是否会对朋友做出亲社会的行为？

sentences.en: Are you more likely to help, to share? Or are you more likely to get into arguments and fights?
sentences.zh: 你更倾向于伸出援手、乐于分享，还是更容易陷入争吵和冲突？

sentences.en: All of it predicted by emotional intelligence.
sentences.zh: 这一切，都能由情商预测出来。

sentences.en: So, I'm sure everyone listening knows of someone who everyone wants to be their friend, because they listen well, they empathize, they reflect feelings, they seem to be able to pick up on something about you that many others don't.
sentences.zh: 所以，我相信每个正在收听的人，都认识这样一种人：大家都想和他做朋友，因为他很会倾听，很有同理心，能够体察并回应别人的情绪，似乎总能捕捉到别人身上一些很多人都注意不到的东西。

sentences.en: And they seem to be able to kind of walk a mile in your shoes.
sentences.zh: 而且，他们似乎总能设身处地为你着想。

sentences.en: And not surprisingly, they are the kinds of individuals who you would love to have as a friend.
sentences.zh: 毫不意外，这样的人正是那种你会渴望拥有的朋友。

sentences.en: You've also looked at how emotional intelligence makes a difference in other realms of life.
sentences.zh: 你还研究过情商在生活其他领域中所产生的影响。

sentences.en: Young people who are more emotionally intelligent tend to be less likely to engage in risky behaviors.
sentences.zh: 情商更高的年轻人，往往更不容易做出冒险行为。

sentences.en: Why do you think this might be the case, Peter?
sentences.zh: 彼得，你觉得这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right. We've shown correlations between Mesquite scores and the likelihood of using drugs or alcohol, particularly in adolescents.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。我们发现，MSCEIT 得分和使用毒品或酒精的可能性之间存在相关性，尤其是在青少年身上。

sentences.en: Higher scores on the Mesquite predict less likelihood of drug or alcohol use, less likelihood of delinquent behavior.
sentences.zh: MSCEIT 得分越高，使用毒品或酒精的可能性就越低，做出不良行为的可能性也越低。

sentences.en: I think some of it is, you know, if you're more in touch with your own emotions, you don't need, what would I say, illicit substances to help you regulate them.
sentences.zh: 我想，部分原因在于，如果你更能觉察自己的情绪，你就不太需要，怎么说呢，借助违禁物质去帮自己调节情绪。

sentences.en: You're less likely to need to self-medicate.
sentences.zh: 你就没那么需要靠“自我用药”来解决问题。

sentences.en: Similarly, if you're better able to empathize, better able to understand the emotions of another person, you're less likely to have conflict with them, less likely to think the way to settle differences is through fighting.
sentences.zh: 同样地，如果你更擅长共情、更能理解他人的情绪，你和别人发生冲突的可能性就更低，也更不容易认为解决分歧的方式就是打架。

sentences.en: Maybe most importantly, you're more likely as a kid to stay in school, because you like school and you like learning better.
sentences.zh: 也许最重要的一点是，作为孩子，你更有可能留在学校里，因为你喜欢学校，也更享受学习。

sentences.en: So I think it's all of a piece, right? You're happier in the school environment, more likely to make friends, less likely to become frustrated, drop out, more likely to not self-medicate with drugs or alcohol when you get older.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这其实是一整套连锁反应，对吧？你在学校环境里更快乐，更容易交到朋友，也更不容易感到沮丧或辍学，长大后也更不容易靠毒品或酒精来“自我治疗”。

sentences.en: It's all of a piece.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是环环相扣的。

sentences.en: And this is not just when you are looking at the behavior of students and young people.
sentences.zh: 而这不仅仅体现在学生和年轻人的行为上。

sentences.en: You find emotional intelligence plays a role in our work lives.
sentences.zh: 你会发现，情商在我们的职场生活中同样扮演着重要角色。

sentences.en: For sure. One small study we did was at an insurance company, where we measured traditional intelligence, we measured personality, and we also gave them a skeet, our measure of emotional intelligence.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。我们做过一项小型研究，是在一家保险公司里进行的，我们测量了传统智力、测量了性格，同时也给他们做了 MSCEIT，也就是我们的情商测量工具。

sentences.en: And what we predicted a time later were the performance reviews you received from your boss, and whether you were likely to get a promotion, and how big a raise that you received at work.
sentences.zh: 而我们后来所预测的，正是你从上司那里得到的绩效评价，以及你是否有可能获得晋升，还有你能拿到多大的加薪幅度。

sentences.en: But the emotional intelligence test that we used, the skeet, was a good predictor of those kinds of workplace outcomes.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，我们使用的这项情商测验，也就是 MSCEIT，能够很好地预测这些职场结果。

sentences.en: People who are better able to regulate their own emotions were at a huge advantage in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 那些更善于调节自身情绪的人，在职场上拥有巨大的优势。

sentences.en: You've written and talked quite a bit about what an emotionally intelligent manager looks like, Peter.
sentences.zh: 彼得，你写过、也谈过不少关于“情商高的管理者是什么样子”的内容。

sentences.en: What are the qualities of individuals in the workplace, and what are they able to do in their interactions with others?
sentences.zh: 在职场中，这样的人具备哪些特质，他们在与他人互动时又能做到什么？

sentences.en: So the emotionally intelligent manager, they recognize what might be going on in a situation beyond what people are simply saying.
sentences.zh: 情商高的管理者，能够察觉出一个情境中超越表面言语的部分。

sentences.en: They recognize that somebody might be saying one thing but feeling another, and that that needs to be explored in depth.
sentences.zh: 他们能意识到，有人嘴上说的是一回事，心里感受到的却是另一回事，而这一点需要被进一步探究。

sentences.en: But I could tell you a story. In early days, David Caruso and I were doing some training at a large investment bank.
sentences.zh: 不过，我可以给你讲一个故事。早些年，我和大卫·卡鲁索一起在一家大型投资银行做培训。

sentences.en: And this was before the Great Recession.
sentences.zh: 那是在经济大衰退之前。

sentences.en: And this was a bank that was quite affected by the Great Recession.
sentences.zh: 而这家银行后来正是受大衰退冲击很深的一家银行。

sentences.en: And these were essentially vice presidents and senior vice presidents engaged in banking, engaged in trading, engaged in providing investment advice and the like.
sentences.zh: 参加培训的，基本上都是从事银行业务、交易业务、投资咨询等工作的副总裁和高级副总裁。

sentences.en: And only 10% of them or so were going to be promoted to their ultimate goal, which was to become a managing director, which is where much more serious compensation is received.
sentences.zh: 而其中只有大约10%的人，最终能晋升到他们的终极目标——成为董事总经理，也就是薪酬待遇远远更丰厚的那个位置。

sentences.en: And so we would ask at the beginning of our conversations, at the beginning of our sessions, how many of you feel that you are above average in IQ?
sentences.zh: 所以，在每次交流或每次培训一开始，我们都会问：你们当中有多少人觉得自己的智商高于平均水平？

sentences.en: And every hand would go up. Then we'd say, how many of you feel that you have strong analytic, or mathematical, or economic skills for your jobs?
sentences.zh: 每次所有人都会举手。然后我们会问：你们当中有多少人觉得自己具备胜任这份工作所需的分析能力、数学能力或经济学能力？

sentences.en: And every hand would go up. We'd look at them and say, I don't understand.
sentences.zh: 每次也都是所有人举手。这时我们就会看着他们说，我不太明白了。

sentences.en: You all are above average in IQ. You all feel you have the analytic, and economic, and mathematical skills to do your job.
sentences.zh: 你们所有人智商都高于平均水平，你们所有人都觉得自己具备胜任这份工作的分析能力、经济学能力和数学能力。

sentences.en: And yet, 90% of you are not going to get to be managing directors.
sentences.zh: 可最终，你们中90%的人是当不上董事总经理的。

sentences.en: What is that all about? And they would say, well, I guess some people are better able at inspiring others.
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？于是他们就会说，嗯，我想大概是有些人更擅长激励别人吧。

sentences.en: Some people are better able to manage their own emotions.
sentences.zh: 有些人更擅长管理自己的情绪。

sentences.en: Some people are better able to manage a group's emotions.
sentences.zh: 有些人更擅长调动一个团队的情绪。

sentences.en: Some people are more charismatic. And they'd start to generate what it meant to be an emotionally intelligent person in that context.
sentences.zh: 有些人更有魅力。于是他们就开始逐渐说出，在那个情境下，一个情商高的人应该具备什么样的特质。

sentences.en: And recognizing that that was the differentiator, not the analytic skills.
sentences.zh: 也开始意识到，真正的分水岭在于这些，而不是分析能力。

sentences.en: Everybody was smart.
sentences.zh: 每个人都很聪明。

sentences.en: I understand, Peter, that some research has also employed brain scanning to study the brain activity of people as they solve emotion-related problems.
sentences.zh: 彼得，我了解到，还有一些研究采用了脑部扫描技术，来研究人们在解决与情绪相关的问题时的大脑活动。

sentences.en: In the study that you're referring to, we ask people to solve problems that were social in nature, problems about conflict with others and the like.
sentences.zh: 在你提到的这项研究中，我们让被试者去解决一些社会性质的问题，也就是关于与他人产生冲突之类的问题。

sentences.en: And maybe the most important aspect of that work is it has seriously challenged the idea that cognition and emotion are separate.
sentences.zh: 而这项研究最重要的意义之一，或许在于它有力地挑战了“认知与情绪是彼此分离的”这一观念。

sentences.en: You can see in fMRI scans that the parts of the brain thought to be involved in emotion and the parts of the brain thought to be involved in thinking, in decision-making, in problem-solving, in creativity.
sentences.zh: 在功能性磁共振成像扫描中你可以看到，大脑中被认为负责情绪的部分，和被认为负责思考、决策、解决问题、创造力的那些部分。

sentences.en: Are closely connected, that there's dense and multiple connections among them.
sentences.zh: 彼此之间联系紧密，存在着密集且多重的神经连接。

sentences.en: And that when you activate what we would think of as a strictly cognitive activity, you're also activating the emotion side of things.
sentences.zh: 而且，当你激活一项我们通常认为纯属认知的活动时，你同时也在激活大脑中与情绪相关的那些区域。

sentences.en: You also can study people with different kinds of brain damage, people who've had strokes, for example.
sentences.zh: 你也可以去研究那些大脑受过不同类型损伤的人，比如中风患者。

sentences.en: And if those strokes affect the emotional parts of the brain, they also have an impact on their thinking.
sentences.zh: 如果那次中风影响到了大脑中与情绪相关的部位，也同样会影响到他们的思维能力。

sentences.en: Emotions provide us with useful information, crucial data points that we can use to inform our responses and our decisions.
sentences.zh: 情绪为我们提供了有用的信息，是我们用来指导自身反应和决策的关键数据点。

sentences.en: Yet people vary widely in their ability to identify, understand and manage emotional signals.
sentences.zh: 然而，人们在识别、理解和管理情绪信号的能力上，却存在很大差异。

sentences.en: Is this capacity innate and fixed, or an ability we can cultivate?
sentences.zh: 这种能力究竟是与生俱来、固定不变的，还是一种我们可以后天培养的技能呢？

sentences.en: When we come back, how to sharpen our emotional intelligence?
sentences.zh: 节目稍后回来，我们将聊聊如何磨练我们的情商。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain. I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是 Hidden Brain，我是 Shankar Vedantam。

sentences.en: Great. Already in there. Approved. Thanks.
sentences.zh: 很好，已经进去了，通过了，谢谢。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain. I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 这里是 Hidden Brain，我是 Shankar Vedantam。

sentences.en: Have you had times in your life when you or someone you know handled a situation with exquisite emotional intelligence?
sentences.zh: 在你的人生中，你有没有过这样的经历：你自己，或者你认识的某个人，以极其精湛的情商处理了某个局面？

sentences.en: Or can you think of a moment when you were, well, an emotional idiot?
sentences.zh: 又或者，你能想起某个时刻，自己表现得，嗯，简直像个“情感白痴”吗？

sentences.en: If you have a personal story you'd be willing to share with the Hidden Brain audience, please find a very quiet room and record a voice memo on your phone.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意和 Hidden Brain 的听众分享你的亲身故事，请找一个非常安静的房间，用手机录一段语音备忘录。

sentences.en: Two or three minutes is plenty. Email the file to us at feedback at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 两三分钟就足够了。把音频文件发送到 feedback at hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: Use the subject line emotional intelligence.
sentences.zh: 邮件主题请写“情商”。

sentences.en: Again, that's feedback at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 再说一遍，地址是 feedback at hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: Peter Salovey is a psychologist at Yale University.
sentences.zh: 彼得·萨洛维是耶鲁大学的一位心理学家。

sentences.en: He studies how our emotions shape our decisions and our behavior.
sentences.zh: 他研究的是我们的情绪如何塑造我们的决策和行为。

sentences.en: Peter, researchers have developed a program intended to help people increase their emotional intelligence.
sentences.zh: 彼得，研究者们开发出了一套项目，旨在帮助人们提升自己的情商。

sentences.en: It's called RULER. I understand this is an acronym.
sentences.zh: 它叫做 RULER。我理解这是一个首字母缩写。

sentences.en: What does it stand for? So RULER is an acronym developed by Mark Brackett, who's a professor here at Yale in the Child Study Center.
sentences.zh: 它代表的是什么呢？RULER 是由马克·布拉克特提出的一个缩写词，他是耶鲁大学儿童研究中心的一位教授。

sentences.en: Happened to have been my postdoc and my collaborator Jack Mayers' graduate student years and years ago.
sentences.zh: 他也恰好曾是我的博士后，同时也是我的合作者杰克·迈耶多年前的研究生。

sentences.en: And RULER is an acronym for the skills that he and his colleagues teach kids from kindergarten through high school to become more emotional, intelligent human beings.
sentences.zh: RULER 是一个缩写，代表的是他和他的同事们，从幼儿园到高中，教给孩子们的一系列技能，目的是让他们成长为情商更高的人。

sentences.en: The first R is recognizing emotion, the ability to know what you're feeling, know what another person is feeling, to recognize emotions through nonverbal cues or verbal ones.
sentences.zh: 第一个R是“识别情绪”，也就是知道自己此刻的感受，知道另一个人的感受，能够通过非语言线索或语言线索来识别情绪的能力。

sentences.en: The U is understanding emotion. What does this emotion mean?
sentences.zh: U是“理解情绪”。这种情绪意味着什么？

sentences.en: How does it transition in time? How does it progress?
sentences.zh: 它会如何随时间转变？它会如何演进？

sentences.en: How do small emotions like irritation turn into big ones like rage?
sentences.zh: 像烦躁这样的小情绪，是如何演变成愤怒这样的大情绪的？

sentences.en: How does it affect our thinking and our behavior?
sentences.zh: 它又是如何影响我们的思维和行为的？

sentences.en: What does it motivate us to do? The L is labeling emotions.
sentences.zh: 它会驱使我们去做什么？L是“标注情绪”。

sentences.en: Can I use words to describe this emotion to others?
sentences.zh: 我能不能用语言把这种情绪描述给别人听？

sentences.en: Can I reflect someone's feeling back to them using words?
sentences.zh: 我能不能用语言，把别人的感受反馈给他们？

sentences.en: Can I identify where emotion words might fit into an emotion space defined by pleasant and unpleasant dimension and an active versus calm dimension?
sentences.zh: 我能不能判断出某个情绪词，在一个以“愉悦-不愉悦”维度和“活跃-平静”维度所定义的情绪空间里，应该被放在什么位置？

sentences.en: Most emotions and feeling states can be mapped onto those dimensions.
sentences.zh: 大多数情绪和感受状态，都可以被映射到这两个维度上。

sentences.en: The E is expressing emotion. What am I showing on my face when I express an emotion?
sentences.zh: E是“表达情绪”。当我表达一种情绪时，我的脸上会显现出什么？

sentences.en: How do I modulate those expressions when I am in different settings, at work versus at home, at a funeral versus at a party?
sentences.zh: 在不同的场合，比如工作场合和家庭场合，葬礼和派对，我又该如何调节这些表达方式？

sentences.en: Am I aware of cultural differences in the way emotions are expressed?
sentences.zh: 我是否意识到，不同文化在情绪表达方式上存在差异？

sentences.en: It's another part of all of this. Do I understand that in certain cultures, weeping openly is perfectly acceptable, and others, a more stoic attitude is expected, or that expressing great joy at one's accomplishment might be perfectly acceptable in America, but a little embarrassing in a place like Japan.
sentences.zh: 这也是其中很重要的一部分。我是否理解，在某些文化中，公开哭泣是完全可以接受的，而在另一些文化中，人们期待的是更为克制的态度；又或者，在美国，对自己的成就表现出极大的喜悦可能完全没问题，但在日本这样的地方，可能就会显得有点尴尬。

sentences.en: The final R is regulating emotion. And this is the area of emotional intelligence that has received the most research attention.
sentences.zh: 最后一个R是“调节情绪”。这也是情商研究中，受到最多关注的一个领域。

sentences.en: A wonderful researcher named James Gross, for example, at Stanford University, who is studying the way in which we manage our emotions, primarily through cognition, for decades and decades.
sentences.zh: 比如斯坦福大学一位很出色的研究者詹姆斯·格罗斯，他几十年来一直在研究，我们主要是通过认知手段来管理自己情绪的方式。

sentences.en: And regulating our emotion, we need to remember we're regulating our emotion, but we also want to regulate the emotions of others sometimes.
sentences.zh: 在调节情绪这件事上，我们需要记住，我们不仅要调节自己的情绪，有时候也希望能够调节别人的情绪。

sentences.en: Why might I want to cheer myself up? Well, perhaps because I'm going to do something creative.
sentences.zh: 我为什么会想让自己振作起来呢？也许是因为我接下来要做一些需要创造力的事情。

sentences.en: Why might I want to calm myself down? Actually feel less happy?
sentences.zh: 我为什么会想让自己冷静下来，甚至有意让自己不那么开心呢？

sentences.en: Well, because I might have a task in front of me where I need to be vigilant and careful and slow.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那可能是因为我面前有一项任务，需要我保持警觉、谨慎和从容。

sentences.en: For example, proofreading a manuscript. What about others?
sentences.zh: 比如说，校对一份稿件。那别人的情绪呢？

sentences.en: When I give a talk, why might I want to tell a joke at the beginning of that talk?
sentences.zh: 当我做演讲时，为什么会想在开场讲个笑话呢？

sentences.en: To manage other people's, regulate other people's emotions before they have to listen to me.
sentences.zh: 为了在听众听我讲话之前，先去管理、调节他们的情绪。

sentences.en: So, ruler is recognizing, understanding, labeling, expressing, and regulating.
sentences.zh: 所以，RULER 代表的是：识别、理解、标注、表达和调节。

sentences.en: And it forms five kinds of skills that you might want to teach to school children as they learn about their emotions.
sentences.zh: 它构成了五类技能，是我们可能想要教给在校儿童、帮助他们认识自身情绪的技能。

sentences.en: And it more or less maps on to the four domains that the Mesquite, which is our ability-based emotion test, measures.
sentences.zh: 而且，它和 MSCEIT（也就是我们基于能力测试的情商工具）所测量的四个维度，基本是能够对应上的。

sentences.en: We organize them slightly differently than ruler, but you can see the overlap very clearly.
sentences.zh: 我们组织这些维度的方式和 RULER 略有不同，但你能非常清楚地看出两者之间的重叠。

sentences.en: I understand that when people ask you how they might improve their own emotional intelligence, you have a couple of practical suggestions for them.
sentences.zh: 我了解到，当人们问你该如何提升自己的情商时，你会给出几条实用的建议。

sentences.en: And one sounds like advice from an English teacher, which is to read good literature.
sentences.zh: 其中一条听起来像是英语老师会给的建议，那就是：多读一些优秀的文学作品。

sentences.en: Why would reading help us increase our emotional intelligence, Peter?
sentences.zh: 彼得，为什么阅读能帮助我们提升情商呢？

sentences.en: Well, it is an interesting question, because one of the things we know is that your emotional intelligence can be improved.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是个很有意思的问题，因为我们知道的一件事是，你的情商是可以被提升的。

sentences.en: It's one of the reasons people love the concept of emotional intelligence, is because unlike IQ, which is kind of difficult to change very much after you're a teenager, you can improve your emotional intelligence over the course of your lifetime.
sentences.zh: 这也是人们喜欢“情商”这个概念的原因之一，因为和智商不同——智商在你过了青春期之后就很难再有太大变化——你的情商却可以在整个人生历程中不断提升。

sentences.en: Merely aging and gaining life experience typically improves your emotional intelligence.
sentences.zh: 光是随着年龄增长、积累人生阅历，通常就能提升你的情商。

sentences.en: Kind of amazing that way. Now, the difference in terms of how we would go about improving our intelligence, our emotional intelligence, concerns whether we're talking about kids or adults.
sentences.zh: 这一点还挺神奇的。至于我们该如何着手提升自己的情商，这种情商，在孩子和成年人身上是有区别的。

sentences.en: For kids, teaching these skills directly in the classroom, as part of a social-emotional learning program, is probably a pretty effective and efficient way to learn these skills.
sentences.zh: 对孩子来说，作为社会情感学习项目的一部分，在课堂上直接教授这些技能，可能是一种相当有效、高效的学习方式。

sentences.en: It's a little more difficult as adults to take a class in emotional intelligence.
sentences.zh: 但对成年人来说，专门去上一堂“情商课”就没那么容易了。

sentences.en: And so we have to look for other ways to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们得去寻找别的途径。

sentences.en: I believe, I don't have a lot of data on which to base this, but I believe that's where the arts can really help us.
sentences.zh: 我相信——虽然我手上没有太多数据支撑这个判断——我相信，艺术在这方面能真正帮到我们。

sentences.en: So imagine that when we're reading great literature and trying to understand the motives of characters and why someone is behaving as they are, why they might behave in ways that look conflicted, all of that helps us develop a more sophisticated understanding of emotions, a greater ability to recognize emotions and label them, and maybe even manage them.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，当我们阅读伟大的文学作品，试图理解书中人物的动机，理解他们为什么会做出某些行为，为什么他们的行为看起来充满矛盾时，这一切都有助于我们发展出对情绪更精细的理解，提升我们识别和标注情绪的能力，甚至可能提升我们管理情绪的能力。

sentences.en: I think having experiences where you're looking at visual art, looking at, let's say, at paintings in an art museum and reacting to them emotionally might help.
sentences.zh: 我认为，去欣赏视觉艺术，比如说，在美术馆里看画作，并对它们产生情绪上的反应，也可能会有帮助。

sentences.en: In Santander, Spain, there is an entire museum, organized art museum, organized around the idea of emotions and creativity.
sentences.zh: 在西班牙的桑坦德，有一整座美术馆，就是围绕“情绪与创造力”这个主题来组织策划的。

sentences.en: Using the art museum experience to practice your emotions.
sentences.zh: 利用美术馆的观展体验，来练习感受和运用自己的情绪。

sentences.en: I think listening to music is a great way to practice feeling emotions that you might not feel that often in the outside world.
sentences.zh: 我认为听音乐也是一种很好的方式，可以让你练习去感受一些你在现实生活中不常体验到的情绪。

sentences.en: I particularly like theater, and when I was in high school, I was an actor.
sentences.zh: 我尤其喜欢戏剧，我上高中的时候，还当过演员。

sentences.en: And I often think theater is a wonderful way, because you're watching behavior, to gain a deeper understanding of what it means to feel an emotion and how it's connected to thinking and behavior.
sentences.zh: 我常常觉得，戏剧是一种很好的途径，因为你在观看的是行为本身，这能让你更深入地理解一种情绪意味着什么，以及它是如何与思维和行为相连的。

sentences.en: In method acting, one of the techniques you might use to create an emotion is actually to enact the behaviors associated with that emotion, and then that emotion might follow.
sentences.zh: 在方法派表演中，你用来创造某种情绪的一种技巧，其实是先去做出与那种情绪相关的行为，然后那种情绪就可能随之而来。

sentences.en: Act as if crying, and crying might follow.
sentences.zh: 先做出哭泣的动作，哭泣的情绪也许就会随之而来。

sentences.en: Well, having those kind of experiences, either as an observer or actually being on stage yourself might help you learn, develop a more sophisticated understanding of how our emotions work, and how they're connected to behavior and cognition.
sentences.zh: 而拥有这样的经历，无论是作为观众，还是真正站在舞台上，都可能帮助你学习，帮助你发展出对情绪运作方式更为细致的理解，理解情绪是如何与行为和认知相连的。

sentences.en: You know, I'm thinking about the times when we go to a gym and we start working with different equipment, and all of a sudden you realize that you had muscles that you didn't know that you had, because your body starts to ache and pain in different places.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在想那种情形：我们去健身房，开始使用不同的器械，突然之间你会发现，原来自己身上有些肌肉是你以前都不知道存在的，因为你的身体开始在不同的部位感到酸痛。

sentences.en: And in some ways, what you're talking about emotions is actually not that different, that in some ways, the more we exercise our emotional repertoire, the more we discover that we have emotional recesses almost, that we haven't really I think that's exactly right, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 而在某种程度上，你所说的关于情绪的这些，其实也没有太大不同——从某种意义上说，我们越是锻炼自己的情绪“肌群”，就越会发现，自己身上还藏着一些我们从未真正……我觉得你说得完全正确，Shankar。

sentences.en: And the more you do it, the better you develop these skills, so that empathizing becomes natural, so that recognizing emotions in someone who is saying something different than they're feeling becomes more second nature, so that you develop over time muscles that allow you to take advantage of the data that is inherent in our emotional system.
sentences.zh: 而且，你练习得越多，这些技能就发展得越好，于是共情就会变得自然而然，识别出一个人嘴上说的和心里感受到的不一样，也会变得更加得心应手，久而久之，你就会锻炼出一种“肌肉”，让你能够利用我们情绪系统里蕴含的数据。

sentences.en: And it becomes, I don't want to sound too woo-woo here, but it becomes kind of like a sixth sense.
sentences.zh: 而它会逐渐变成——我不想说得太玄乎——但它会变得有点像一种“第六感”。

sentences.en: Yes, we see and we hear and we taste and we smell and we touch.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们能看、能听、能尝、能闻、能触摸。

sentences.en: But we also feel our emotions. And maybe there's some data there that is being conveyed to us that we should pay attention to.
sentences.zh: 但我们同样也能感受我们的情绪。也许其中传递给我们的一些数据，是我们应该去留意的。

sentences.en: Why is it that I'm thinking about, well, let's say purchasing a product, but I get a feeling in the pit of my stomach that's a little queasy?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样：我正在考虑，比方说，买一件商品，却在胃里感到一阵隐隐的不适？

sentences.en: Shouldn't I stop and think about why that product made me feel that way?
sentences.zh: 我难道不应该停下来想一想，这件商品为什么会让我产生这种感觉吗？

sentences.en: Why is it that I might find myself attracted to another person and that's accompanied with joy versus it's accompanied by a little bit of worry?
sentences.zh: 为什么我会发现自己被另一个人吸引，而这种感觉伴随的是喜悦，还是伴随着一丝担忧呢？

sentences.en: What does that tell me? What does that tell me?
sentences.zh: 这告诉了我什么？这又告诉了我什么？

sentences.en: And so for the most part, people go through life ignoring all of that.
sentences.zh: 而在大多数情况下，人们对这一切都视而不见，径直走过。

sentences.en: And what I'm suggesting is these are data.
sentences.zh: 而我想说的是，这些都是数据。

sentences.en: And when you ask a friend, let's say, or spouse or family member to roleplay something with you, tomorrow I'm going to go ask my boss for a raise.
sentences.zh: 当你请一位朋友，比如说，或者配偶、家人，和你一起做角色扮演——比如，明天我要去找老板谈加薪的事。

sentences.en: When you roleplay it, you learn how expressing certain words create certain feelings in you.
sentences.zh: 当你进行这种角色扮演时，你会学到，说出某些话语会在你心里激发出怎样的感受。

sentences.en: You learn when your feelings are maybe going to push you in directions you don't want to go.
sentences.zh: 你会明白，自己的情绪有时会把你推向你并不想去的方向。

sentences.en: And you can practice modulating those feelings.
sentences.zh: 而你也可以借此练习调节这些情绪。

sentences.en: You can practice regulating them. You can practice taking a deep breath, pausing, giving yourself a minute to calm down, and then continuing on.
sentences.zh: 你可以练习去调控它们。你可以练习深呼吸，暂停片刻，给自己一分钟平静下来，然后再继续。

sentences.en: Our whole conception of emotional intelligence is that these are skills.
sentences.zh: 我们对情商的整体理解是：这些都是可以习得的技能。

sentences.en: You use the metaphor muscle. You can think of these as skills, just like an athletic skill, where, you know, when you develop those muscles and you take thousands and thousands of foul shots from the basketball foul line, you get better at them.
sentences.zh: 你用了“肌肉”这个比喻。你可以把它们看作一种技能，就像运动技能一样——当你锻炼这些“肌肉”，投出成千上万次罚球时，你自然会越来越擅长。

sentences.en: The same is true when you roleplay emotionally evocative situations.
sentences.zh: 当你在情绪上练习模拟那些能引发强烈感受的情境时，道理也是一样的。

sentences.en: What can I learn from watching the way my body responds, my thoughts change, and my feelings are expressed and have an impact on others?
sentences.zh: 从观察自己的身体反应、思维变化，以及自己的情绪表达并对他人产生影响的过程中，我能学到什么？

sentences.en: The idea of emotional intelligence isn't new.
sentences.zh: “情商”这个概念其实并不新鲜。

sentences.en: In fact, you might say it's one of the most popular terms in all of psychology.
sentences.zh: 事实上，可以说它是整个心理学领域里，最流行的术语之一。

sentences.en: Managers, parents, teachers, all preach the importance of emotional intelligence.
sentences.zh: 管理者、家长、老师，都在不断强调情商的重要性。

sentences.en: Sadly, however, a lot of what you may have heard about this concept is wrong.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，你所听到的关于这个概念的很多说法，其实是错误的。
